source: GLWA Incident Report 2022: Executive Summary (p.4-6), Section 4.2 cause statement (p.17, stripped), Conclusions (p.20), Recommendations (p.21), Pure Technologies conclusions (p.147, 177). Withheld or stripped.
question: Cause of the 2022 GLWA 120-inch PCCP main break and changes to prevent or limit a repeat.

items.engineers: Failure was not caused by a pressure increase or surge: the main broke at normal operating pressure, below its 200 psi design pressure, with no high-pressure fluctuations recorded before the break.
leak_phrases: did not appear to be caused by an increase in system pressures

items.engineers: Probable cause: the mortar coating was degraded by the environment, allowing corrosion plus hydrogen-embrittlement damage of the prestressing wire; loss of wires in this vintage (1968-71) PCCP leads to sudden catastrophic rupture.
leak_phrases: combination of corrosion and hydrogen embrittlement
mortar coating being adversely affected by the environment

items.engineers: No unacceptably distressed pipe found beyond the three 16-ft lengths replaced; 31 pipes with 5-25 broken wire wraps (4 of 204 east, 27 of 1,248 west) are left in service for monitoring.
leak_phrases: no unacceptably distressed pipe beyond the three pipe segments

items.engineers: Perform unmanned in-service electromagnetic assessment of the whole 120-inch main (Pure Technologies PipeDiver) since it cannot be taken out of service easily.
Consider lowering the operating pressure of the 120-inch main (up to 200 psi) to prolong the life of the asset.
leak_phrases: lowering the operating pressure of the 120-inch transmission main

items.engineers: Keep the backup supply path: re-evaluate decommissioning of the Northeast WTP, which allowed NSC to pump north through the 96-inch main; review emergency operating procedures with GCDC and Flint (emergency connection / FL-01 valve issues).
leak_phrases: re-evaluating the proposed decommissioning of the Northeast WTP
improvements to the emergency operations procedures
